title: Deploy-gated-interpretability-and-SNR-thresholds-for-Optimize-evals
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Add an additional, model-agnostic gate to Optimize evals that combines lightweight interpretability checks with cohort-level signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) thresholds. This gate acts as an early-warning filter before traffic ramp and as a fast-stop signal during canaries. Motivation: existing eval gates rely largely on scalar regression thresholds and A/B delta checks. We need a complementary signal that catches model regressions that are subtle but actionable: increased response variance (low SNR) or loss of explanation coherence (failed interpretability checks) that correlate with user-visible quality drops. This ticket defines requirements, measurement formulas, rollout constraints, and rollback triggers for the new gate. Scope: - Define interpretable, automatable checks (saliency sanity, attribution sparsity, hallucination keyword heuristics) that can run on prompt sets and live canary traffic. - Specify cohorting rules for SNR computation (by prompt intent, token-length, latency bucket). - Define SNR formula and percentile-based thresholds for gating. - Describe how interpretability and SNR signals compose into a composite gate (AND/OR weighting), and how they interact with existing Optimize eval signals (A/B delta, safety fails). - Define observability (dashboards/alerts) and runbook actions for gate failures. Out of scope: building new heavy-weight attribution pipelines; full model explainability UI (this ticket only requires programmatic checks and alerts).
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible SNR calculation is documented and implemented on the offline promptset harness: SNR = |mu_delta| / sigma_delta where delta is per-prompt quality score improvement relative to baseline; formula doc link included.
Cohorts: at minimum 'intent', 'length_bin', and 'latency_bucket' cohorts implemented; SNR computed per cohort and at global level.

Interpretability checks: three lightweight heuristics implemented and runnable on sample promptsets: (1) saliency distribution sanity (no extreme concentration shift), (2) attribution sparsity ratio (fraction of tokens with >X attribution), (3) hallucination-keyword hit-rate change. Each check emits pass/fail and a numeric score.
Composite gate behavior documented and implemented: gate trips if (global SNR < threshold) OR (>=2 interpretability checks fail on the same cohort); the logic parameterized for future tuning.
A canary rollout config is added to Console: default canary size 5% traffic, evaluation window 1 hour, automatic stop if gate trips within window; can be overridden by release owner.
Observability: dashboard with cohort-level SNR timeseries, interpretability check pass rates, and a summarized composite_gate boolean; alert to #optimize-eval on gate trip within 5 minutes.
Runbook: clear remediation steps for engineers and PMs, including immediate rollback, scoped traffic reduction, and triage checklist.
End-to-end test: a simulated regression (PRD-provided failure case) triggers the gate in staging and prevents >80% of a planned canary traffic ramp when run against the configured 5% canary.
success_metrics: False positive rate of gate on historical known-good rollouts < 5%.
True positive detection of historical regressions (from past incidents) >= 80%.
Median time-to-detect from canary start for injected regressions < 12 minutes.
Reduction in production rollbacks that require hotfixes (by count) versus prior quarter by 20% (longer-term metric).
rollout_plan: Week 1: Spike/POC — research team implements SNR and interpretability checks on offline promptsets and runs against last 6 months of eval data. Deliverable: analysis doc with recommended thresholds.
Week 2: Implement hooks in Optimize eval harness and add composite gate logic as feature flag behind 'eval_gates:interpret_snr_v1'. Deliverable: feature-flagged pipeline + unit tests.
Week 3: Internal staging canary — enable gate for 5% synthetic canaries; monitor false positive/negative signals and tune thresholds. Deliverable: staging dashboard and tuning notes.
Week 4: Gradual roll to production: enable for internal customers only, then to 10% customer canaries, with manual approve to expand. Deliverable: production dashboard + runbook verified.
Fallback plan: if gate exhibits high false positive rate during roll, automatically disable the gate via feature flag and roll forward previous config while investigating.
risks: Risk: SNR may be unstable for very small cohorts. Mitigation: only evaluate cohorts with Ns > 50 or fallback to aggregate-level SNR.

Risk: Interpretability heuristics can be brittle across model families. Mitigation: baseline heuristics per model family and conservative default thresholds; require research sign-off for new model onboarding.
Risk: Extra eval compute may increase cost and latency for continuous eval jobs. Mitigation: run interpretability checks as a sampling job (20% of prompts) and schedule heavier checks off-peak.
Risk: Alert fatigue if gate trips frequently on noisy signals. Mitigation: dual-threshold (soft warning vs hard stop) and require 2+ failing cohorts for hard stops.
decisions: Use SNR definition: SNR = abs(mean_delta)/std(delta) computed over per-prompt quality scores; use bootstrap to compute 95% CI for robustness.
Composite gate policy: default to OR semantics (low SNR OR multi-check interpretability fail) for immediate safety; allow later switch to weighted scoring.
Minimum cohort size threshold set to 50 prompts; cohorts below this size use global SNR only.
Default canary: 5% traffic, 1 hour evaluation window, minimum 1000 prompts to evaluate cohort signals; feature-flag controls for release owners.
